source.title: Sparse Autoencoder Decomposition of Clinical Sequence Model Representations: Feature Complexity, Task Specialisation, and Mortality Prediction
source.authors: Chris Sainsbury; Feng Dong; Andreas Karwath

record.tranche_reason: Applies sparse-autoencoder decomposition to a clinical sequence model, a new model setting, and reports feature-structure and cross-seed reproducibility results.
record.gate_note: The paper measures SAE reconstruction, feature complexity, and feature reproducibility. Its mortality and length-of-stay probes evaluate clinical prediction utility, while its warfarin-to-INR interventions evaluate a downstream association; those outcomes do not directly measure the representational properties named by the claim versions. The study does not test toy-model superposition geometry, neuron-level feature distribution, or feature dimensionality.
record.test_reason: Trains TopK SAEs on a 14.5M-parameter clinical-code transformer (not an LLM). It reports sparse reconstruction quality and cross-seed feature stability, bearing on V4 (recoverable sparse dictionary features) and V5 (stability) in a new setting. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that representations become more abstract with depth and that SAE features are only about 21% reproducible across seeds, so individual features are illustrative only. They add that SAE features beat dense representations for mortality only under full-sequence probes; at leakage-safe windows, dense representations match or exceed SAE features.
record.recipe_differences: Uses TopK SAEs on residual-stream activations of a clinical sequence model; the study does not reproduce toy-model superposition experiments or measure their geometric transition.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature complexity and reconstruction vary across transformer depth; feature matching declines with depth.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE feature complexity rises with depth: from near-token detectors at layer 0 to features spanning about 30 token types at layer 6.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features become more abstract and multi-token with transformer depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Under full-sequence probes, SAE features beat dense representations for mortality but lose for length of stay. At leakage-safe windows, dense representations match or beat SAE features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse decomposition discards continuous-magnitude information and can lose predictive signal relative to dense activations.

record.code_released: https://github.com/csainsbury/ascend-flat (currently private; contact the corresponding author for collaborator access)
record.problems: Evidence comes from one 14.5-million-parameter model. Cross-seed feature reproducibility is low, and the authors did not formally quantify seed-wise variability of downstream results. Category coherence uses coarse clinical categories and is not a demonstration of monosemanticity. No neuron-level or feature-direction geometry is measured.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable for the version-specific feature-structure and reproducibility results recorded. Mortality/length-of-stay prediction and warfarin-to-INR perturbation results were not included because they assess downstream task utility or effects, not the representational properties named by the tested versions.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweep, phase transition or geometry.
No test of capacity competition or importance-based allocation.
Not an LLM. No neuron-level distribution of features, and no comparison of SAE EV with dense or low-rank baselines.
Completeness and canonicality across methods or dictionary sizes are not tested. Only seed stability is tested.

missing.what: EV under the hyperparameter sweep (expansion 4/8/16 × K 8/16/32): EV 0.67-0.94, driven by K.
Mean cosine of matched features across seeds (0.91 to 0.78, declining with depth).

record.verdict_notes: The subject is a GPT-2-style model over clinical codes, not an LLM, so the V4 verdicts are a new-setting extension. The layer-0 EV rows are uninformative because the vocabulary is smaller than the dictionary. The 30% LLM reproducibility figure is cited from Paulo & Belrose, not measured here. The record's own V5 label was challenges with partial row states; here challenges rests on the authors' explicit instability statement.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-over-capacity sweep, sparsity-dependent transition, or overlapping/nearly orthogonal direction geometry.
Does not test whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition or whether importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Does not test polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of their occurrence.
Tests SAE decomposition in one clinical sequence model, not LLMs; does not measure distribution across neurons or compare feature directions with orthogonal directions.
Measures cross-seed reproducibility, but does not establish feature completeness or canonicality across methods, models, or training data.
Does not test whether the model's underlying features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional features.

relationships.condition: FlatASCEND clinical transformer, layers 3-9, INSPECT and MIMIC-IV, TopK K=16, 8x expansion
relationships.reason: An overcomplete TopK SAE with 16 active features recovers 85-92% of variance (r2-r4, r6-r8), with category-coherent features (r17, r18).
relationships.display_finding: With 16 active features, the overcomplete TopK SAE recovered 85–92% of variance, and its features were coherent with clinical categories.

relationships.condition: INSPECT layer 6 across SAE K and expansion; coarse-category interpretability
